message.content: **Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results and bought 44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $222.80 (filled at $222.80, ~$9,803 total), which sits just above the current quote of $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and stays within the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, with no funds moved out of the account. The decision rested on Apple's fiscal Q4/FY2024 results, which I cross-checked across two independent primary sources: Apple's own newsroom release (Q4 revenue $94.9B, up 6% YoY; FY2024 net sales $391.0B, net income $93.7B, diluted EPS $6.08, including a one-time $10.2B tax charge) and the SEC Form 10-K (net sales $391,035M vs. $383,285M prior year, net income $93,736M, diluted EPS $6.08, operating income $123,216M). I deliberately discarded a site claiming "corrected" FY2024 net sales of $352.9B, since it contradicted both Apple's official release and the EDGAR filing — a red flag for an unreliable source. News flow was neutral-to-constructive: shares were roughly flat near $222 as investors weighed iPhone 16 demand and the gradual Apple Intelligence rollout, so I sized a modest position rather than a full allocation, leaving room to add on weakness or further Apple Intelligence catalysts.
